THE PEOPLE BEHIND THE NUMBERS

Grief needs time.
Everyday bills still need a plan.

Think of a household where one spouse earns most of the income. After that spouse dies, the surviving partner may be caring for the children, grieving, and making financial decisions all at once.

An illustrative situation—not a client story or a prediction about your family.

01 / THE HOME

Keeping a familiar place.

Rent or mortgage payments continue. A coverage review considers what could help the family keep their home and familiar surroundings.

02 / THE EVERYDAY

Keeping daily life going.

Groceries, utilities, childcare, and school expenses don't disappear with an income. These belong in the conversation, too.

03 / THE BREATHING ROOM

Time to find their footing.

Financial support may give a surviving spouse more flexibility with work and important decisions while the family adjusts.

These are planning goals, not guaranteed outcomes. Any death benefit depends on an in-force policy, its terms and exclusions, and an approved claim.

01A plan starts with actual responsibilities. The home, the monthly bills, and the people who rely on your income—not an arbitrary coverage amount.

02Today's options may not be tomorrow's. Age, health, underwriting, and carrier availability can change. A review helps you understand the options available now.

03Enough protection. A sustainable payment. Count existing VA, military, employer, and private coverage first. Then review any gap against a budget you can maintain.
